implementation_notes: The runtime shape is JavaScript's - resolve a Recipient[] per message, then settle every delivery with Promise.allSettled - but TypeScript makes the computed list checkable: a discriminated union for recipient kinds (channel, topic, webhook), a branded identifier so an unresolved name cannot reach deliver(), and a resolver signature (msg: Message) => Promise<Recipient[]> that forces recipient resolution to be an explicit, testable step. The type system adds no runtime primitive, so it does not replace the classic structure; it only turns mis-wired fan-out into a compile error. Hand-written router classes remain justified when policy has to be injected as a component rather than closed over.
pitfalls: structuredClone drops class instances, functions and custom prototypes, so a typed message class silently loses behaviour when copied per recipient.
Typing recipient identifiers as plain string lets a tenant id or an unresolved name flow into deliver(); a branded RecipientId makes that a compile error.
A discriminated union only narrows if every member carries its tag literally - widening kind to string in an interface disables the checks the fan-out relies on.
